newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Judge got 5yrs pay for not sitting on bench - Bruton.
newsitem.headline: Judge got 5yrs pay for not sitting on bench - Bruton.

text.p: A judge was paid full salary for over five years for not hearing any cases, Irish prime minister John Bruton told parliament on Wednesday, as a debate on a motion of no confidence in the government continued.

But Bruton said that had occurred when the main opposition party was in government. It was only one of three problems with judicial appointments by that government and none of their ministers had resigned over these "administrative difficulties". Neither had there been any inquiry into those problems.

The judge in question had been paid for just over five years, without hearing a case, after it was found that he had not been a barrister long enough to qualify for appointment to the bench. the Department of Justice to tell a judge that the Cabinet had removed him from one of the most sensitive courts in the land - the Special Criminal Court, which deals with terrorist offences.

The judge had remained on the bench for over three months after the Cabinet removed him. That resulted in 16 prisoners having to be released from jail and immediately re-arrested. Further legal action by those men against the State is expected.

Bruton said the Inquiry team set up to investigate the treatment of the removal of the judge was free to interview anybody, including the Attorney General Dermot Gleeson and the Director of Public Prosecutions and their officials.
